Title: The clock is running out on Bitcoin's $200k dreams in 2025

Summary: 
With fewer than 100 days left in 2025, Bitcoin is trading at just over $109,000, roughly 12% below its August all‑time high. The "supercycle" narrative is fraying amid persistent Fed rate‑hike threats, U.S. political gridlock, fiscal uncertainty, and potential forced liquidations. More cautious upper bounds from VanEck ($180,000), Matrixport ($160,000), and Peter Brandt ($150,000 floor) now appear more realistic, and a correction into the $90,000 zone cannot be ruled out. Title: Bitcoin and Gold Jump as Stocks Dip Amid US Government Shutdown

Summary: 
Bitcoin rose 3.6% in the last 24 hours to $117,293, reaching its highest price in about two weeks, and surged over 7% since Sunday, while gold hit a new all-time high above $3,922 per ounce—recently priced at $3,902, up 4.6% in the past week—amid a stock market downturn caused by the U.S. government's first shutdown in nearly seven years. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to $6,658, and the Nasdaq composite dropped 0.5% to $22,530 at market open, though indices later recovered slightly. The shutdown, which began at midnight on October 1, 2025, halted most federal agency functions, including economic data collection. Analyst Eric Balchunas of Bloomberg noted that Bitcoin may be decoupling from the stock market, a trend he views as positive for institutional investors seeking portfolio diversification. He cited expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve rate cut—'almost guaranteed'—as a potential driver. Balchunas emphasized that zero correlation with equities, like gold, could significantly increase Bitcoin’s long-term valuation. Market sentiment remains bullish, with Myriad estimating a 65% probability that Bitcoin will surpass $125,000 before falling to $105,000. The last U.S. shutdown, in late 2018, lasted 35 days and caused the S&P 500 to drop over 9%—its worst December since 1931.

Title: Cryptos Dip As Data Dents Rate Cut Hopes

Summary: 
Stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data on Thursday dampened hopes of an immediate Fed rate cut, boosting the dollar and weighing on crypto markets. Cryptocurrency market capitalization fell 2% overnight to $3.75 trillion, though 24‑hour trading volume rose 31% to $231 billion. Market focus shifts to Friday’s PCE inflation readings, with headline PCE expected at 2.7% and core at 2.9%. Overall, crypto market cap declined nearly 2% in 24 hours, while Bitcoin trades about 12% below its all‑time high of $124,457.12 set on August 14.
